concerns.text: Task T001 is tagged `[P1]` (parallel‑safe) but it creates project directories and fetch‑data scripts that are required by subsequent tasks (e.g., T002). Running it in parallel with any other task would cause race conditions, violating the `[P]` guarantee.

Task T002 is also marked `[P1]` yet it depends on the outputs of T001 (fetch functions, config). It cannot be safely executed in parallel with T001 or any other task that writes to the same `data/`/`outputs/` locations.

Task T003 carries `[P2]` but consumes the processed DataFrame produced by T002. Parallel execution with T002 (or any task that modifies `data/processed/clean.parquet`) would break the producer‑consumer ordering.
Task T004 is marked `[P2]` yet it requires the cleaned dataset from T002 and the species list produced earlier. It must run after those producers, so the `[P]` tag is inaccurate.
Task T005 is labeled `[P2]` but performs a likelihood‑ratio test against the OLS model generated in T004. It therefore has an implicit ordering dependency on T004 and cannot be parallel‑safe.

Task T007 (sensitivity analysis) is `[P2]` yet it re‑runs correlation analysis, OLS CV, and RF CV using results from T003, T004, and T006. It must wait for those tasks, so the parallel‑safe tag is misleading.
Task T008 (power analysis) is `[P2]` but depends on the PGLS result from T005. It cannot be executed in parallel with T005.
Task T009 is marked `[P3]` yet it validates all artifacts produced by earlier tasks. It must run after every producer; the `[P]` annotation is therefore incorrect.
Task T010 (report generation) is `[P3]` but assembles a report that references the validation results from T009 and all analysis JSONs. It cannot be parallel‑safe.
